reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This bill expands specified benefits programs for veterans and their survivors and establishes a supplemental monthly allowance for certain disabled veterans. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act (H R 1041)
votes.bill_title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act
votes.plain_language: This bill prohibits the Department of Veterans Affairs from transmitting certain information to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System utilized by licensed importers or dealers of firearms. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act (H R 1041)
votes.bill_title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 1041 (Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act) prohibits the Department of Veterans Affairs from transmitting certain information to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System utilized by licensed importers or dealers of firearms. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Fiscal Year 2025 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act (S 2393)
votes.bill_title: Fiscal Year 2025 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, during FY2026. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes (S 4465)
votes.bill_title: A bill to amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until June 12, 2026. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act (S 1318)
votes.bill_title: Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act
votes.plain_language: This bill carries the Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act and the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act as passed by the House; it reauthorizes Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until April 30, 2029, with added protections related to Section 702, and bars Federal Reserve banks from issuing a central bank digital currency or offering accounts directly to individuals. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ernest Peltz Accrued Veterans Benefits Act (H R 3123)
votes.bill_title: Ernest Peltz Accrued Veterans Benefits Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes procedures for the Department of Veterans Affairs to issue a pension that was due but unpaid at the time of a veteran’s death. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Veterans Readiness and Employment Improvement Act (H R 980)
votes.bill_title: Veterans Readiness and Employment Improvement Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill removes the requirement that educational and vocational counseling services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs on campus at institutions of higher learning must be provided by VA counselors. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act (S 629)
votes.bill_title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill revises the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program to expand eligibility for payments to agricultural producers and owners of forest land impacted by natural disasters. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. It was a pleasure to welcome EPA Administrator @LeeMZeldin to Rockland County for a roundtable discussion on New York’s energy policies and the energy and environmental challenges facing our state.
 
We discussed ways to lower energy costs, strengthen reliability, and protect our environment. Hudson Valley families and businesses deserve affordable, reliable energy, and I’ll keep working to deliver it.

Proud to welcome Federal Highway Administration Administrator Sean McMaster to Putnam County to highlight progress on the $10 million safety improvement project at Stoneleigh Avenue and Drewville Road near Putnam Hospital.

The project includes a new roundabout, improved sightlines, upgraded drainage and other enhancements to improve traffic flow and safety for residents, patients, hospital staff and first responders.

I’ve worked with local, state and federal partners to advance this project and secure the federal investment needed to make it happen. I’ll continue fighting for the infrastructure improvements our Hudson Valley communities deserve.

This week, I visited Stepping Stones, the historic home of Bill and Lois Wilson in Katonah.

Bill Wilson, co-founder of Alcoholics Anonymous, and Lois Wilson, co-founder of Al-Anon Family Groups, left a lasting legacy of support and recovery for individuals and families affected by alcoholism.

Thank you again for the warm welcome and for providing a tour of this historic and significant site.

I am deeply saddened by the passing of Donald R. “Cool Breeze” Branson of Stony Point and extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, and loved ones.

A proud United States Army veteran and longtime member of Charles R. Lewis VFW Post 8997 in Tomkins Cove, Donald devoted himself to supporting fellow veterans and serving the Stony Point community.

From helping lead the town’s Memorial Day parades to his instrumental role in establishing the veterans memorials at Routes 9W and 210, Donald worked to ensure that our nation’s heroes would always be remembered.

His presence at community gatherings and veterans ceremonies will be deeply missed, but his legacy will live on through the many lives he touched. Rest in peace, Cool Breeze. Thank you for your service and your unwavering commitment to our veterans and community.

Lowering the cost of living means tackling the policies driving it up. From tax cuts and housing legislation to permitting reform, we’re working to make life more affordable for hardworking New Yorkers. https://t.co/kGsx3GSfwT

Grateful that law enforcement, acting on a tip from an individual, stopped a white supremacist’s plot to attack a Hindu temple outside Chicago before anyone was hurt. My colleague Raja Krishnamoorthi and his family were worshipping there that day.

Places of worship must be safe for everyone. White supremacy and all forms of extremism have no place in America.

https://t.co/7zo8ra2AwG

Heartbroken by the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.

My prayers are with the families, the entire community, and those stolen from us far too soon.

Today, I welcomed FHWA Administrator Sean McMaster to Putnam County to highlight critical safety improvements coming to the Stoneleigh Avenue and Drewville Road intersection near Putnam Hospital. After years of work, we’re moving this $5 million project toward construction to make our roads safer for patients, families, first responders, and everyone who travels here.

It was great to visit the Italian American Club of Mahopac and present proclamations in recognition of their contributions to our community. 

Thank you for your continued dedication to preserving Italian American heritage and bringing our community together. https://t.co/AhlBLB6D17

Americans deserve transparency and accountability in our elections. That means having clear rules to prevent candidates from using campaign coordination arrangements to get around finance limits.

Right now, coordination between political campaigns and super PACs can allow candidates to circumvent contribution limits and benefit from unlimited spending. 

The Stop Illegal Super PAC Coordination Act would help close these loopholes, strengthen campaign finance rules, and protect the integrity of our elections.

As the new school year gets underway, it was great to visit with students, teachers, and staff at Hendrick Hudson School in Westchester! 

Our schools play such an important role in preparing the next generation for success, and I’m grateful to the educators who work hard every day to support our students. 

Wishing everyone a successful school year filled with learning, growth, and new opportunities!

Last year, I had the opportunity to visit with @Pontifex at the Vatican to discuss America’s role in the world and Pope Leo XIV’s historic ascension to the papacy.

Doina and wish him a speedy recovery at he battles lung cancer and keep him in our prayers.

May God Bless him. https://t.co/W7KtllLQMm

My office was proud to attend the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the Monsey Fire Department’s Chief Hugh Jacobson Fire Training Center, honoring the legacy of Hugh “Chaim” Jacobson.

For nearly three decades, Chaim served his community as a volunteer firefighter, demonstrating unwavering dedication to protecting his neighbors and keeping fellow firefighters safe. This training center stands as a tribute to his life of service and lasting impact on the Monsey community. May his memory be a blessing.

We owe it to Holocaust survivors and the families of victims to ensure the full truth is uncovered. 

Following the discovery of hundreds of previously undisclosed accounts with potential ties to the Nazi regime, I’m urging the Treasury Department to reopen its investigation into Credit Suisse. We must ensure transparency, accountability, and that this history is never forgotten.

Today, we celebrate the 251st birthday of the United States Navy and honor the brave men and women who have served and continue to serve our nation. For 251 years, our Navy has defended our freedoms and protected our country with courage and dedication. Thank you to all who serve and have served. Happy birthday to the U.S. Navy!

It was a pleasure to join Ken Lester, Claudine Dugue, Sedrick Dugue, and so many others in support of the Critical Accident Relief Foundation (CARF).

Founded by Claudine after she experienced a serious accident, CARF helps individuals and families facing the financial hardships that often follow a life-changing accident by providing emergency assistance and resources when they need them most.

Here in the Hudson Valley, we know the importance of looking out for one another, especially during difficult times. I would like to thank CARF for all that they do.

Last week, the Scouting America Greater Hudson Valley Council Awards were held at Camp Bullowa.

Congratulations to all the award recipients on this well deserved recognition, and thank you to everyone who continues to support Scouting and help develop the next generation of leaders in our community.

My office was proud to attend the 4th Annual Latina Voices event during Hispanic Heritage Month, hosted in partnership between Dominican University and 100 Hispanic Women of Rockland.

Thank you to both organizations for bringing the community together to celebrate Latina voices and contributions!

Happy Columbus Day! Today is an opportunity to celebrate Italian American heritage and recognize the generations of Italian Americans who have helped shape our nation and strengthen our communities. https://t.co/TypzEU1dQ8

Congratulations to the Rockland County Shields on 60 years. It was great to celebrate this milestone and recognize the organization’s longstanding commitment to supporting law enforcement and our community. Here’s to many more years of service and success! https://t.co/DWfTIWk8kF

As a proud member of Leo Laders American Legion Post 130, I was happy to join everyone in Thiells for a wonderful Wine & Dine evening! Thank you to everyone at Post 130 for put together a great event and made it such a great night for our Post community. https://t.co/DYEKvXMNdR

I had a great time celebrating the Briarcliff Manor Fire Department’s 125th anniversary! Thank you to all the firefighters and volunteers who have dedicated their time and service to keeping our community safe for generations. Congratulations on 125 years of service, and here’s to many more!

Since the tragic loss of her daughter Melanie in 2022, Cheryl has turned unimaginable heartbreak into a mission to protect other families and prevent them from experiencing the same tragedy.

It was especially meaningful to join the Melanie Chianese Foundation, survivors, advocates, community organizations, and law enforcement in the Town of Wappinger for a special Community Day for Domestic Violence Awareness to support victims of domestic violence and their families.

Cheryl’s tireless advocacy helped make Melanie’s Law a reality in New York, expanding protections for vulnerable family and household members. I’m proud to support bringing those same protections to families nationwide through federal legislation.

Proud to join Congressman Josh Gottheimer to introduce the bipartisan Lauren Shields Organ Donation Act. This legislation honors Lauren’s legacy by making it easier for Americans to register as organ donors and helping save lives for generations to come.

Lauren dedicated her life to giving others hope, and this bill will help carry that legacy forward and bring hope to the thousands of Americans waiting for a life-saving transplant.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
